live_web_research.page_text: [2610.12469] Rubric-CEPR: Self-Evolving Image Editing via Reward-Verified Self-Distillation Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition arXiv:2610.12469 (cs) [Submitted on 8 Oct 2026] Title: Rubric-CEPR: Self-Evolving Image Editing via Reward-Verified Self-Distillation Authors: Ritesh Thawkar , Shubham Patle , Shravan Venkatraman , Rao Muhammad Anwer View a PDF of the paper titled Rubric-CEPR: Self-Evolving Image Editing via Reward-Verified Self-Distillation, by Ritesh Thawkar and 3 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Instruction-guided image editors have become highly capable, yet improving them further still depends on human-edited training pairs or external reward models. Such supervision is costly to obtain and can reward plausible failures: a realistic output may leave the requested change undone or alter content that should be preserved. In this work, we strive to improve a pretrained image editor using only its own generations, without human-edited targets or an external training-time reward model. To this end, we propose a self-evolving framework, named Rubric-CEPR, that verifies the editor's own samples with its internal representations through a rubric-augmented Contrastive Edit-Preservation Reward (CEPR). A Planner proposes structured edit instructions from unlabeled images, the Editor samples multiple candidate edits, and a frozen Critic scores each candidate with decomposed rubric checks for edit realization, removal of the old state, and content preservation, using features already exposed by the editor. Non-compensatory gates reject infeasible candidates, and the best verified candidate is distilled into the editor through lightweight adapter training. On Qwen-Image-Edit, Rubric-CEPR improves ImgEdit from 4.36 to 4.60 (+5.5%), with a +24.9% gain on object isolation, and transfers to GEdit-Bench and Complex-Edit. The same procedure also improves Step1X-Edit by +7.8% on ImgEdit. We hope our approach will serve as a solid baseline for image editors that improve themselves from their own verified samples. Automated self-improvement is the focus of Rubric-CEPR, a new method for image editing that uses self-distillation. The system evaluates its own edits against a specific rubric and uses that feedback to evolve without human labeling. This type of self-evolving architecture is the most viable path to reducing the massive overhead and human-bottlenecks associated with fine-tuning specialized generative models. article.body:
Title: Google Shifts Gemini Toward Agentic AI for Enterprise Users

Google is transitioning its Gemini platform from conversational tools to autonomous systems that execute multi-step business workflows. This move addresses the "productivity plateau" where simple chat interfaces fail to deliver measurable ROI.

Google is building the software agents, while new research in "world models" and safety filtering suggests a parallel push to make AI more reliable in physical robotics. The industry is hitting a ceiling with text generation, forcing a pivot toward action-oriented systems.

Google has integrated agentic capabilities into Gemini for businesses, aiming to automate complex tasks across its software suite. Researchers have published DreamTrue, a robot world model using counterfactual post-training to improve mechanical reliability in unpredictable environments.

Enterprise adoption rates for Google's agents compared to Microsoft's Copilot stack and the transition of "world models" from research papers to commercial factory floor applications are key areas to watch. Regulatory scrutiny of tech executive spending in upcoming election cycles is also significant.
